subtype: Approach: protecting mental health while the storm passes [Thinking]
passage: Saturday. Day one of no notifications. A big page mocked my video and the comments have been ugly, and yesterday I checked the numbers every hour and felt sick each time. Today I muted everything for two days and left the phone in the drawer. Went to the market with Amma, then sat on the balcony with my sister Himani while she peeled peas, and I told her the worst comment. She said, 'Who wrote it? A stranger who won't remember you next week.' That helped more than I expected. I keep telling myself attention moves on and that what people I've never met say isn't the measure of me. Still stings a bit. I'll look on Monday, once. — Bhupen

qa.q: For how long did Bhupen mute notifications?
qa.a: Bhupen muted them for two days.

qa.q: How did Bhupen feel when checking the numbers every hour?
qa.a: Bhupen felt sick each time, and now feels calmer though it still stings a bit.

qa.q: What could Bhupen do if the mocking carries on for longer?
qa.a: Bhupen could ask Himani or another trusted person to watch for real problems and mention only what needs an answer.

qa.q: How might Himani have felt hearing the worst comment?
qa.a: Himani was probably concerned and wanted to reassure, reminding Bhupen that a stranger would not remember it next week.

grounding: Shows a person muting notifications, avoiding hourly checks and talking with family while reminding themselves that strangers do not define their worth.
